_doc: How each bedrock formation breaks, for the terrain's rock shaping (docs/rock-rules.md). One rule per formation, matched to the geology grid by class id. Read by src/level.js (not yet: the plan is in docs/rock-rules.md and waits on Matt). Azimuths and strikes in degrees clockwise from north; dips in degrees from horizontal; lengths in metres. 'source' says where each number comes from: lidar (tools/rock_calibrate.py, USGS 3DEP ME MidCoast 2021), the existing veneer, or a starting guess for Matt to correct in the field.

apply._doc: Where the rules shape the ground. Outcrop = any of these; everywhere else the surface is left as surveyed.
apply.note: Within mesh_within_m the vertices move (the 1 m rings); out to normals_within_m only the shading follows the rule; beyond, nothing. max_displacement_m caps how far the rule may move the surveyed surface, so the lidar shore line stays where it is.

formations.name: Bar Harbor Formation (and the state map's metasedimentary rocks)

bedding.source: strike from lidar: the parallel ribs at Compass Harbor trend 25-55 deg (steep-face strike peaks 25 and 55); dip and dip direction are a starting guess, not measurable at 1 m. Correct in the field.

joints.source: lidar: steep faces on the Shore Path strike 125-165 deg; scarp spacing at Compass Harbor ~3 m (weak). Part of that is the shoreline itself.
guess: a set along the bedding strike

step.source: guess: below what 1 m lidar resolves (risers under ~1 m are invisible in it)

jitter._doc: how far each block's step is pushed up or down (x step height), how far its edges wander off the joint plane; no two ledges repeat

formations.roughness_source: lidar: 0.27 m rms at 4 m on the Shore Path shore band (0.38 at Compass Harbor)

overhangs.where: riser height > 1.2 m facing the sea
overhangs.source: rule for Assets' rock pieces; the height map cannot overhang

loose_blocks.where: foot of risers > 0.8 m, below MHW+1

formations.name: Cadillac, Somesville, Southwest Harbor and the Devonian granites

sheeting.source: existing veneer (spacing 2.2 m, curvature 0.6); lidar preferred-step 4.9 m at Otter Cliffs is too weak (autocorrelation 0.21) to calibrate it

joints.source: lidar: the strongest steep-face strike at Otter Cliffs is 0-10 deg (also the veneer's N-S set)
lidar: second peak at 105-125 deg at Otter Cliffs; the veneer had 60 deg (the dike trend). Changed to what the lidar shows; the dikes keep their own trend.

ice._doc: stoss (up-ice) sides smoothed and polished, lee sides plucked into steps

formations.roughness_source: lidar: 0.67 m rms at 4 m on the Otter Cliffs shore band

overhangs.where: lee-side risers > 2 m and sea cliffs

loose_blocks.where: foot of cliffs and risers > 1.5 m; boulder-beach habitat

joints.source: guess, near the Compass Harbor rib trend

formations.name: Ellsworth Schist (and schist/gneiss of the state map)

foliation.source: guess; no schist shore in the lidar patches yet

formations.name: Cranberry Island volcanics, tuff and lava, shatter-zone breccia
basalt, diabase and aplite dikes
formations._doc: dikes weather differently from their host: basalt/diabase into trenches (dark, recessed), aplite into ribs (pale, standing proud)
